===Etymology 1===
{{clipping|en|Lawrence}}.

====Proper noun====
{{en-proper noun|s}}

# {{surname|en|from=patronymics}}.
# {{given name|en|male|dimof=Lawrence}}.
#: {{cot|en|Laws|Laus|Lars|Lau|Lar|Lawry|Laury|Larry|Laurence|Lawrence}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{der|en|ang|hlaw||a hill or burial mound}}.

====Proper noun====
{{en-proper noun|~}}

# {{surname|en|[[topographic]]|from=Old English|addl=perhaps originally meaning someone who lives near a [[burial mound]]}}.
# {{lb|en|Scotland}} a conical hill
# {{place|en|village|carea/South Lanarkshire|cc/Scotland|c/UK}} {{q|[[OS]] grid ref NS8252}}.

=====Further reading=====
* {{pedia|lang=en|Law, South Lanarkshire}}

===Etymology 3===
A [[semantic loan]] of Greek  {{m|grc|νόμος||law}}, rendering Hebrew {{m|he|תּוֹרָה||instruction, teaching|tr=tōrāh}} in the sense of divine law.

====Proper noun====
{{head|en|proper noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q34990}} {{lb|en|Judaism}} {{syn of|en|Torah<id:Q34990>}}: the five [[Books of Moses]], particularly the [[commandment]]s in it, as well as their [[specification]] in the [[Mishnah]] and their further [[interpretation]] in later religious literature.
#: {{hyponyms|en|Oral Law|Written Law}}
# {{lb|en|Christianity|biblical}} the commandments in the Books of Moses, sometimes seen as [[transcend]]ed by Christ
# {{lb|en|Christianity|less often}} the commandments and moral principles that are [[binding]] for Christians, such as the [[Decalogue]], the teachings of the [[New Testament]], the [[Church Fathers]], etc.

===Etymology 4===
From {{bor|en|yue|羅}}. {{doublet|en|Luo|Lo}}.

====Proper noun====
{{en-proper noun}}

# {{surname|en|from=Chinese}}.

===Statistics===
* According to the 2010 United States Census, ''Law'' is the 1,089<sup>th</sup> most common surname in the United States, belonging to 32,122 individuals. ''Law'' is most common among White (65.61%), Black (15.63%) and Asian (14.22%) individuals.
